0283_labeling_video_writer.schema.json.title: Labeling video writer Native authority
0283_labeling_video_writer.schema.json.$comment: Migration 0283 adds a fixed Labeling finalizer for claimed video executions. It validates the exact current Jobs proof before receipt replay, reconstructs candidate prefixes from immutable Jobs checkpoints, fences Mask keys in bounded batches, and atomically updates the canonical Job, Jobs finish fact, and immutable receipt.

owner_capabilities.semantics: Immutable, no canonical Job foreign key, unique by operation and logical run.

prepare.semantics: Checks the current proof before replay, then returns canonical Job and accepted input facts. Matching immutable receipts bypass restaging.

lock_masks.semantics: Keys must be unique and globally C-sorted. Existing Labeling Mask write authority is acquired in batches of 1000 inside the caller transaction; permits accumulate across batches.

apply.semantics: Revalidates the current claim, checkpoint-derived results, accepted evidence, stage identity and actual Mask references before atomically publishing Job status, Jobs finish fact and immutable receipt.

read_window.semantics: Returns the byte-verified original UTF-8 payload and manifest plus only the current-generation attempt.

read_publication.semantics: Read-only current-proof lookup of the immutable publication for this Job and run, including an earlier command generation. Exact status digest matching remains unchanged.

has_track_results.semantics: Derives nonempty sealed track output from byte-verified canonical window payloads.

0295_labeling_project_counter_write.sche.title: Labeling Project counter projection write
0295_labeling_project_counter_write.sche.$comment: This SQL function is a bounded bridge for caller-owned ORM flushes. It writes only the changed Labeling-owned counter columns and does not recalculate, authorize, take extra read locks, or commit.

functions.semantics: Apply only supplied counter columns in the caller's transaction. Unknown fields and patches without a counter column raise 22023. PostgreSQL column types retain int32 and JSONB validation. updated_at becomes now() unless explicitly supplied. Return the target Project UUID or null when the row no longer exists. The caller owns authorization, flush ordering, rollback, and commit.

0299_labeling_project_counter_deltas.sch.title: Labeling Project counter deltas
0299_labeling_project_counter_deltas.sch.$comment: Fixed caller-transactional counter updates. Functions perform only the corresponding Labeling counter fields and updated_at write; actor policy and commit remain with the caller.

functions.semantics: Execute one UPDATE of review_tasks = GREATEST(COALESCE(review_tasks, 0) - 1, 0) and updated_at = now() for the matching Project. A matched row is updated even when the counter is already at zero. SQL NULL input executes the UPDATE and matches zero rows, returning SQL NULL like a missing Project. The attempted UPDATE is still rejected in a read-only transaction. Native int32 overflow propagates as PostgreSQL SQLSTATE 22003. The UPDATE uses normal row-update waiting. No actor checks, extra locks, other writes, or commit are added; the caller owns the surrounding transaction.

Execute one UPDATE of completed_tasks = GREATEST(COALESCE(completed_tasks, 0) - 1, 0) and updated_at = now() for the matching Project. A matched row is updated even when the counter is already at zero. SQL NULL input executes the UPDATE and matches zero rows, returning SQL NULL like a missing Project. The attempted UPDATE is still rejected in a read-only transaction. Native int32 overflow propagates as PostgreSQL SQLSTATE 22003. The UPDATE uses normal row-update waiting. No actor checks, extra locks, other writes, or commit are added; the caller owns the surrounding transaction.

Execute one UPDATE of completed_tasks = COALESCE(completed_tasks, 0) + 1, review_tasks = GREATEST(COALESCE(review_tasks, 0) - 1, 0), and updated_at = now() for the matching Project. SQL NULL input executes the UPDATE and matches zero rows, like a missing Project. The attempted UPDATE is still rejected in a read-only transaction. Native int32 overflow propagates as PostgreSQL SQLSTATE 22003. The UPDATE uses normal row-update waiting. No actor checks, extra locks, other writes, or commit are added; the caller owns the surrounding transaction.

0434_prediction_output_ownership.schema..title: Prediction execution output and fixture retirement

functions.aap_jobs_v1.begin_prediction_mask_produc: Commit one exact current Job lease, generation and result ordinal before generated-Mask production.
functions.aap_jobs_v1.bind_prediction_mask_object(: Bind an exact allocated Mask owner under the current generation; reject stale admission.
functions.aap_jobs_v1.finish_prediction_mask_produ: Settle the producer only after its prepared result is sealed and its caller has completed physical work.
functions.aap_jobs_v1.prediction_mask_object_retai: Retain an exact object while any bound producer remains pending.
functions.aap_assets_v1.fixture_prediction_inputs_: Prove exact fixture original identities and the absence of retained original-read operations after fixture sealing.
functions.aap_jobs_v1.fixture_prediction_retired(u: Return true only for a birth-bound terminal prediction Job with terminal native execution and retry receipts, completed managed scopes, qualified input and settled output owners; false or error blocks.
functions.aap_jobs_v1.guard_fixture_prediction_led: Lock the project Job and failure scope and require each related retry attempt and delivery to have the exact retirement proof.

invariants: Pending or uncertain producer intents and allocated object identities survive worker loss and block cleanup.
Fixture Job birth identities prevent resurrection after deletion; Job deletion atomically snapshots dispatch intents without claiming broker drain.
Retry attempts, delivery receipts, execution facts and completed managed scope retirements remain independent tombstones.
